<explanation>
1. Project type and purpose
   - Kopia is an open-source, full-stack backup and restore tool combining:
     • A command-line client (CLI)  
     • A graphical Electron-based UI  
     • A repository server exposing gRPC/HTTP APIs  
     • A Go-library "core engine" implementing snapshot, encryption, deduplication, compression, upload, and restore logic  
     • Pluggable storage-provider implementations (S3, Azure, B2, GCS, WebDAV, SFTP, filesystem, Rclone)  
     • Notification subsystem (email, webhook, Pushover, JSON)  
     • Documentation site and build tooling  

2. High-level components
   a. User Interfaces  
      • CLI process (main.go + cli/)  
      • Electron UI (app/)  
   b. Core Engine  
      • Snapshot management (snapshot/)  
      • Repository abstraction and content/index/manifest management (repo/)  
      • Crypto, ECC, encryption, hashing, compression subsystems (internal/crypto, repo/ecc, repo/encryption, repo/hashing, repo/compression)  
      • Filesystem abstraction layers (fs/)  
      • Utilities: cache, metrics, parallel work, retry, scheduling, locking, logging (internal/*)  
   c. Repository Server  
      • gRPC & HTTP handlers (internal/server/, internal/grpcapi/)  
      • HTML UI kernel embedded (internal/server/htmlui_*.go)  
   d. Storage Providers  
      • repo/blob implementations: S3, Azure, B2, GCS, filesystem, WebDAV, SFTP, Rclone, sharded, throttling, metrics  
   e. Notification Subsystem  
      • notification/senders and templates (notification/)  
   f. Documentation Site  
      • Hugo-based site (site/)  
   g. Build & Test Infrastructure  
      • Makefiles, CI workflows, test suites, tools/  

3. Relationships & data flows
   - UI (CLI or Electron) → invokes Core Engine API  
   - Core Engine  
     • Snapshot module reads local filesystem (fs/) → builds snapshot manifest → hands off to upload module  
     • Upload module → Repository abstraction → chooses storage provider  
     • Repository abstraction → marshals objects (content, index, manifest) → persists via blob storage driver  
     • Encryption and compression applied in transit  
     • Deduplication ensured by content–addressed content manager  
   - Server mode: CLI/Electron → gRPC/HTTP → server API layer → Core Engine  
   - Notification: Core Engine emits events → notification subsystem sends via configured senders  
   - Restore: reverse flow through repository → content reader → snapshot restore module writes to filesystem  
   - Documentation site built independently  

4. Architectural patterns & design principles
   - Modular Go packages: clear separation of concerns  
   - Dependency inversion via interfaces (storage.Provider, content.Manager, notifier.Sender)  
   - Pluggable backends for storage, encryption, notification  
   - Layered architecture: UI → API → Core → Storage  
   - gRPC+HTTP and plugin pattern for extensibility  
   - Extensive test coverage (unit, end-to-end, stress)  

5. Diagramming guidelines
   - Use distinct shapes/colors:
     • Rectangles for components  
     • Cylinders for storage (cloud buckets, file system)  
     • Rounded boxes for interfaces/APIs  
   - Group related packages as sub-components:
     • Core Engine box containing Snapshot, Upload, Repository, Crypto, FS, Utils  
     • Storage Providers cluster  
     • Notification cluster  
   - Draw directional arrows:
     • UI → Core API  
     • Core → Repository → Storage  
     • Core → Notification → External services  
     • CLI/Electron → (optional) Server → Core  
   - Annotate arrows with protocols or formats (gRPC, HTTP, content blobs, JSON notifications)  
   - Color code layers:
     • UI (blue), API/Server (green), Core Engine (purple), Storage Providers (orange), External Storage (yellow), Notification (teal)

6. Tailoring the diagram
   - Emphasize CLI vs. GUI entry points  
   - Show server mode separately: CLI → gRPC → API CLI handlers → Core  
   - Illustrate pluggable storage drivers hooking into the repo/blob registry  
   - Highlight key subsystems: encryption, deduplication, compression, manifest/index  
   - Optionally include test harnesses and CI pipelines as side-bars

7. Essential elements to include
   - Labels: “CLI Client”, “Electron UI”, “Snapshot Manager”, “Upload Module”, “Repository Abstraction”, “Blob Storage Drivers”, “gRPC/HTTP Server”, “Notification Senders”  
   - Arrows: data & control flow (e.g., “snapshot→upload”, “upload→storage”)  
   - Legend: color/shapes meaning  

By organizing the diagram into these logical layers and components—annotating data flows, protocols, and key Go packages—you will capture Kopia’s full architecture in a clear, accurate, and extensible system design diagram.
</explanation>
